boundary_rationale: Onset: the book opens on two datelines in two counting systems - בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.1.1, a regnal/exilic year the book never names an era for) and הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין (oshb:Ezek.1.2, the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile) - followed at oshb:Ezek.1.3 by the superscription הָיֹ֣ה הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְ֠הוָה אֶל יְחֶזְקֵ֨אל, an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect word-event with a THIRD-PERSON addressee ('to Ezekiel', not 'to me'). This verb and addressee shape are why the verse sits in the 49-verse any-form word-event count and not the 48-verse first-person family (sweep: verses containing the word-event phrase in any form, 49; the 48 excludes this one verse by predicate). It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The same verse also carries וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָֽה, the hand-of-YHWH construct that opens the book's first vision (one of 7 verses carrying the construct). Close: the scene runs unbroken to oshb:Ezek.1.28, מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר, glossed by the WEB as “this was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh's glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke” (web:Ezek.1.28). No word-event, messenger, recognition or utterance formula interrupts 1:4-1:27 (the transport-verb and 'he said to me' sweeps that mark scene changes elsewhere in the book's visions do not begin until chapter 8), so the throne-theophany carries no formula-marked internal seam; the samekh recorded after 1:28 and the fresh 'he said to me' that opens oshb:Ezek.2.1 together mark the vision/commission seam on the FAR side of this unit; the onset evidence at oshb:Ezek.2.1 is weighed there.

Rejected because the vision proper (1:4-1:28) carries no independent onset device of its own - it simply continues the sentence the hand-of-YHWH clause opens - so cutting after 1:3 would manufacture a seam the bytes do not mark, and would still leave a 25-verse remainder with the same cap problem.

device_notes: Whole-chapter span (28 verses), well above the 7-10 typical density and above the 14-16 stretch cap for measured/listed blocks even though this is not such a block; disclosed under the E-02 cap posture and held low rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut. MT 1:3 is cited only under the 49-verse any-form word-event count (never blended with the 48-verse first-person family, per the denominator reconciliation). K/Q at 1:8 checked before quoting: the unit does not splice the disputed word. The OSHB editorial note at 1:11 is disclosed as single-witness apparatus, not a reading change. boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.1 וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן אָדָם֙ עֲמֹ֣ד עַל רַגְלֶ֔יךָ וַאֲדַבֵּ֖ר אֹתָֽךְ ('he said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet”') opens the commission immediately after the vision's samekh-marked close at oshb:Ezek.1.28. The sending proper follows at 2:3, שׁוֹלֵ֨חַ אֲנִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶל (oshb:Ezek.2.3) ('I send you to the children of Israel'), continuing into the messenger formula כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.2.4), embedded as reported speech rather than a fresh onset. Pe marks fall after 2:2 and 2:5, disclosed as intra-row sub-paragraph texture, not unit cuts. Close: 2:7, the refrain-form יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם יֶחְדָּ֑לוּ (oshb:Ezek.2.7) ('for they are rebellious'), with a pe recorded after it, before a fresh sub-onset address opens at 2:8.

device_notes: Pe marks at 2:2 and 2:5 fall inside the unit and are disclosed as sub-paragraph texture (single-witness); neither coincides with a formula onset, so neither is read as a unit-cutting seam. The samekh after oshb:Ezek.1.28 closes the preceding unit's own vision scene and is not this unit's onset evidence.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.8 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם … ('and you, son of man, hear…') opens a fresh sub-onset immediately after the refrain-marked pe close at oshb:Ezek.2.7. The scroll appears at 2:9, וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּה יָ֖ד שְׁלוּחָ֣ה אֵלָ֑י וְהִנֵּה (oshb:Ezek.2.9) ('behold, a hand stretched out to me'), and its inscription is read at 2:10, אֵלֶ֔יהָ קִנִ֥ים וָהֶ֖גֶה וָהִֽי (oshb:Ezek.2.10) ('lamentations, mourning, and woe'), with a samekh recorded after 2:10, disclosed as intra-row texture rather than a cut, since the eating that follows continues the same scroll scene: 3:1 reopens with a further 'he said to me,' אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר (oshb:Ezek.3.1) ('eat this scroll'), intra-row, and the WEB chapter numeral falling at 2:10/3:1 is disclosed only as tier-4 texture, never as boundary evidence (E-23). Close: 3:3, הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֣ן אֵלֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Ezek.3.3) ('it was in my mouth as sweet as honey'), with a pe recorded after it, before the address turns from the scroll to the audience's character at 3:4.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:4 לֶךְ בֹּא֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.3.4) ('go, get you to the house of Israel'), a fresh 'he said to me' turning from the scroll itself to the audience it will be spoken to; 3:7 characterizes them, כִּ֚י כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חִזְקֵי מֵ֥צַח וּקְשֵׁי לֵ֖ב הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.7) ('for all the house of Israel are obstinate and hard-hearted'). A pe is recorded after 3:9, כְּשָׁמִ֛יר חָזָ֥ק מִצֹּ֖ר נָתַ֣תִּי מִצְחֶ֑ךָ ('I have made your forehead as a diamond'), closing with a further רebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּֽית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.9) (the third of six). That mark is disclosed but not read as the unit's own close: 3:10 reopens with 'moreover he said to me' on the same audience-description topic, and cutting there would leave 3:10-3:11 (2 verses, no word-event of its own) below the unit-size floor. Close: 3:11, אִֽם יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם יֶחְדָּֽלוּ (oshb:Ezek.3.11) ('whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse'), immediately before the return-transport of 3:12 begins a distinct, vision-texture scene.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:12 וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ (oshb:Ezek.3.12) ('then the Spirit lifted me up') begins the return-transport away from the plain-vision back to the exiles, distinct in texture from the preceding commissioning speech (no address, no imperative - narrated action). 3:14 carries the hand-of-YHWH construct, וְיַד יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה (oshb:Ezek.3.14) ('the hand of YHWH was strong upon me'); it is weighed and NOT read as a fresh vision onset here, in contrast to 1:3 and 3:22 - it sits inside a single continuous journey (lifted up → went in bitterness → came to Tel-abib) with no scene change around it, so it is disclosed as transit texture rather than a hard seam. Close: 3:15, וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.3.15) ('I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days'); no parashah mark is recorded at 3:15, which is not read as counterevidence against the seam. The gap this closes is temporal, not formulaic: 3:16 reopens on 'at the end of seven days' with its own strict word-event.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:16 carries the book's first strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.3.16) ('at the end of seven days, Yahweh's word came to me, saying'), a hard seam under the frame-spine rule (one of the 39 strict-form verses; also one of the 48 first-person family). A pe is recorded after this verse; the inventory does not carry intra-verse position, so no claim is made about whether the mark falls before or after 3:17's watchman charge, צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.3.17) ('I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel'). A samekh follows 3:19, between the wicked-man case (3:18-19) and the righteous-man case (3:20-21); disclosed as an internal paragraph mark, not a unit cut, since both cases are one paired illustration of the same watchman charge and no fresh onset device stands at 3:20. Close: 3:21, at the second samekh, before the hand-of-YHWH reopens the scene at 3:22.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:22 וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.3.22) ('Yahweh's hand was there on me'), the hand-of-YHWH construct read here as a genuine vision onset (contrast oshb:Ezek.3.14, weighed above as transit texture) because it opens a fresh scene: 'arise, go out into the plain'. 3:25 commands עֲבוֹתִ֔ים (oshb:Ezek.3.25) ('ropes') to be placed on the prophet; the same word recurs at 4:8 on the far side of the assigned parent seam, and is disclosed here as continuity evidence the seam must be weighed against, per the standing cross-seam rule - the muteness command and the sign-acts share a byte-true device even though the unit boundary stands. 3:26 carries the fifth rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה. Close: 3:27, הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.27) ('he who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house') - the sixth and last of the twelve book-wide occurrences of the refrain, and the parent P1's close; a samekh is recorded after this verse. This is the INTERNAL PARENT SEAM named in the launch message: the unit stops here and does not extend into 4:1.

device_notes: Operative-category deviation disclosed: this span also carries commission_narrative texture (the muteness charge proper runs 3:24-3:27 inside this vision-opened scene); labelled vision_report because the unit's onset device is the hand-of-YHWH construct at 3:22. Paseq at 3:27 occurs twice (double occurrence on one verse), disclosed count-only, single-witness. The ropes-word continuity with 4:8 is disclosed per the standing cross-seam rule; it argues for the closeness of the two units, not against the assigned seam standing between them.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) ('you also, son of man, take a tile'), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that opens P2 (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam weighed at oshb:Ezek.3.27 above. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) ('behold, I put ropes on you') recurs the exact word from 3:25 on the far side of the parent seam, disclosed as continuity evidence the seam-assessment above already weighed. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act ('behold, I will break the staff of bread'). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) ('that they may lack bread and water'), with a pe recorded after it, before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 5:1 וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן אָדָ֜ם קַח לְךָ֣ חֶ֣רֶב חַדָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.5.1) ('you, son of man, take a sharp sword'), a fresh 'son of man' sub-onset distinct from 4:1's - a new symbolic object (sword/razor/hair) rather than a continuation of the siege-tile act. The messenger formula at 5:5, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.5.5), opens the act's own interpretation rather than a competing unit (no refrain close intervenes between the hair-sign and its meaning). The oath at 5:11, חַי אָ֗נִי ('as I live'), with the utterance signature נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.5.11) attached mid-verse, marks an emphatic sub-onset of the verdict paragraph, not a unit boundary. The formula 'I, Yahweh, have spoken' recurs three times, at 5:13 (אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ (oshb:Ezek.5.13)), 5:15 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.15)) and 5:17 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.17)); the first two are paragraph-final rather than unit-final because no fresh onset device follows either (5:14 continues 'moreover I will make you a desolation' with no messenger formula or word-event reopening the address). Close: 5:17, with a pe recorded after it, before 6:1 opens with a fresh strict word-event. The verdict continues in two further 'therefore' messenger formulae addressing the same party: 5:7, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.7) (2mp, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says'), and 5:8, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.8) (2fs, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says') — both verdict paragraphs inside the same interpretation, addressing Jerusalem and the people in her as one party, with no refrain standing before either (the samekh after 5:6, 5:7 and 5:9 are disclosed as intra-row texture, not unit-cutting seams). The verdict is bound to the sign-act itself by a byte-identical clause: 5:12 closes with the same words that close 5:2, וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.5.2; oshb:Ezek.5.12) ('and I will draw a sword after them', sweep: 3 verses book-wide, the third at 12:14).

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.1 opens with the dateline וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗ית בַּשִּׁשִּׁי֙ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ אֲנִי֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵיתִ֔י וְזִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים לְפָנָ֑י וַתִּפֹּ֤ל עָלַי֙ שָׁ֔ם יַ֖ד אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (sixth year, sixth month, fifth day) carrying the hand-of-YHWH idiom in its אדני יהוה form (tier-1 vision onset; the construct-only sweep counts 7 hand-of-YHWH verses book-wide, of which this is the only one carrying the double divine name), immediately followed by the transport at oshb:Ezek.8.3 וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ תַּבְנִ֣ית יָ֔ד וַיִּקָּחֵ֖נִי בְּצִיצִ֣ת רֹאשִׁ֑י וַתִּשָּׂ֣א אֹתִ֣י ר֣וּחַ בֵּֽין הָאָ֣רֶץ וּבֵ֣ין הַשָּׁמַ֡יִם וַתָּבֵא֩ אֹתִ֨י יְרוּשָׁלְַ֜מָה בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֶל פֶּ֜תַח שַׁ֤עַר הַפְּנִימִית֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה צָפ֔וֹנָה אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֣ם מוֹשַׁ֔ב סֵ֖מֶל הַקִּנְאָ֥ה הַמַּקְנֶֽה (the Spirit lifts the prophet and sets him at Jerusalem's inner-court gate — tier-1 vision transport, sweep: 20 verses book-wide) and the phrase במראות אלהים 'in visions of God' (sweep: 3 verses book-wide — 1:1, 8:3, 40:2, the three vision-transport frames). Close: oshb:Ezek.8.6 ends the directed “lift up your eyes” scene with וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הֲרֹאֶ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה מהם עֹשִׂ֑ים תּוֹעֵב֨וֹת גְּדֹל֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּֽית יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עֹשִׂ֣ים פֹּ֗ה לְרָֽחֳקָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל מִקְדָּשִׁ֔י וְעוֹד֙ תָּשׁ֣וּב תִּרְאֶ֔ה תּוֹעֵב֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת, the prophet's first sight of the image of jealousy and the promise “you will again see yet other great abominations,” which turns the page to the next scene rather than closing the vision; a samekh follows oshb:Ezek.8.6 (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration to a seam here even though no oracle-refrain formula is present. boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 15:1 opens with the strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.15.1), immediately followed by the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.15.2) at 15:2, which puts the riddle about the useless vine-wood in the standard oracle-onset frame. Close side: the row's final verse, MT 15:8, ends the applied sentence against Jerusalem's inhabitants and carries the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature at its own end, matched by a pe mark recorded on 15:8 in the single-witness paragraph layer. A samekh mark sits earlier, on 15:5 (sweep: 8 verses), where the riddle's own question -- whether the vine-wood, even charred, is fit for any use -- reaches its rhetorical dead end before the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.15.6) opens the application at 15:6. That mid-chapter mark is weighed and not adopted as the row seam: the application (15:6-8) answers the riddle (15:1-5) rather than opening an independent formula-bounded unit of its own, and a three-verse application row would not itself carry a fresh word-event onset. The row is therefore kept as the whole chapter, with the internal mark disclosed rather than acted on.

device_notes: Whole-chapter span disclosed under the E-02 cap posture: MT 15 is 8 verses and is kept as one row rather than split at its internal samekh (15:5, single witness). This span carries no K/Q note, no paseq, and the editorial-note layer is silent across it.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: the word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.16.1) at 16:1, the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.16.2) at 16:2, and the messenger formula naming the addressee, כֹּה אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Ezek.16.3) at 16:3, together open the foundling allegory and fix Jerusalem as the figure's referent from the first clause; the pe recorded at MT 15:8 (single witness) closes the unit before it, corroborating this row's onset from the far side of the seam. Close side: MT 16:14 is this row's last verse, and its own final words are the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.14), closing the first movement (the abandoned infant clothed, fed and enthroned) before the narrative turns to her unfaithfulness at 16:15. No parashah mark falls between 16:1 and 16:14 (sweep: 14 verses), so the utterance-formula close is the only mark-independent boundary evidence available for this stretch, and it is taken as such. MT 16:13 (oshb:Ezek.16.13) carries a doubled Ketiv/Qere note inside this span: the running text reads the ketiv forms ששי and אכלתי in place of the pointed readings; the Qere layer gives (Qere for both) שֵׁ֤שׁ (fine linen) and אָכָ֑לְתְּ (you ate) respectively. Neither Qere is used to argue this boundary; both are disclosed because the span covers them.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: no formula device opens MT 16:15; the row continues the word-event unit framed at 16:1 by default, picking up the narrative turn וַתִּבְטְחִ֣י בְיָפְיֵ֔ךְ וַתִּזְנִ֖י (oshb:Ezek.16.15) ('you trusted in your beauty and played the whore') immediately after 16:14's close. Close side: this row's final verse is 16:19; its concluding clause is the utterance formula וַיֶּ֑הִי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.19) ('so it happened, declares the Lord YHWH'), closing the account of the gifts turned into idol-offerings before the child-sacrifice material opens at 16:20 with its own fresh clause. No parashah mark falls in this five-verse stretch, so the seam rests on the verse-final formula alone (sweep: 5 verses); it is held at less than full confidence for that reason. MT 16:18 (oshb:Ezek.16.18) carries a single Ketiv/Qere note inside this span: the running text reads the ketiv נתתי in place of the pointed form.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:20 opens a sharper escalation with no fresh formula device, וַתִּקְחִ֞י אֶת בָּנַ֤יִךְ וְאֶת בְּנוֹתַ֨יִך (oshb:Ezek.16.20) ('you took your sons and your daughters'), continuing the same word-event unit by default. Close side: MT 16:23 closes the row, and its final clause is the double cry and utterance formula א֣וֹי א֣וֹי לָ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.23) ('woe, woe to you, declares the Lord YHWH'), a verse-final close reached after the summary at 16:22 recalls the days of the addressee's youth. No parashah mark falls in this four-verse stretch (sweep: 4 verses); the seam again rests on the verse-final formula alone. Two single Ketiv/Qere notes fall inside this span: MT 16:20 reads (oshb:Ezek.16.20) the ketiv מתזנתך and MT 16:22 reads (oshb:Ezek.16.22) the ketiv זכרתי.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:24 opens with no fresh formula device, וַתִּבְנִי לָ֖ךְ גֶּ֑ב וַתַּעֲשִׂי לָ֥ךְ רָמָ֖ה בְּכָל רְחֽוֹב (oshb:Ezek.16.24), continuing the word-event unit by default and cataloguing the addressee's promiscuity against Egypt, Philistia, Assyria and Chaldea in turn (16:26-29). Close side: the row is taken through 16:34, whose final clause וַתְּהִ֥י לְהֶֽפֶך (oshb:Ezek.16.34) ('and you became the opposite') closes the reversal-of-a-prostitute's-wages figure just before the summons לָכֵ֣ן זוֹנָ֔ה שִׁמְעִ֖י (oshb:Ezek.16.35) ('therefore, prostitute, hear') opens at 16:35. The utterance formula recurs at 16:30, מָ֤ה אֲמֻלָה֙ לִבָּתֵ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.16.30), but sits mid-verse there, with the clause on the deeds of a brazen prostitute still to follow, so it is weighed and not treated as a row-final refrain. The paragraph layer records a pe on 16:35, one verse AFTER this row's own close at 16:34, not on 16:34 itself; that is disclosed rather than smoothed over, because it means the mark corroborates a seam one verse later than the addressee-shift onset this row's boundary is actually argued from. MT 16:25 (oshb:Ezek.16.25) carries a single Ketiv/Qere note, reading the ketiv תזנתך in the running text. MT 16:31 (oshb:Ezek.16.31) also carries a doubled Ketiv/Qere note inside this span, one of the five flagged doubled-note verses in this chapter: the running text reads the ketivs עשיתי and הייתי, against the Qere readings עָשִׂ֖ית and הָיִ֥ית (oshb:Ezek.16.31, Qere for both); neither Qere is used to argue this boundary.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:35, לָכֵ֣ן זוֹנָ֔ה שִׁמְעִ֖י דְּבַר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.35) ('therefore, prostitute, hear the word of YHWH'), is the addressee-change summons the paragraph layer marks with a pe recorded on this same verse; the messenger formula כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.16.36) completes the introduction at 16:36 and opens the judgment sentence proper. Close side: the row is taken through 16:43, whose own final clause is the plain עַ֖ל כָּל תּוֹעֲבֹתָֽיִך (oshb:Ezek.16.43) ('besides all your abominations'), not a formula refrain -- the utterance formula recurs earlier in the same verse but mid-clause, with this tail still to follow, so it is weighed and not used as the close. The close is instead argued from the fresh default onset that follows: MT 16:44, הִנֵּה֙ כָּל הַמֹּשֵׁ֔ל עָלַ֥יִךְ יִמְשֹׁ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּאִמָּ֖ה בִּתָּֽהּ (oshb:Ezek.16.44) ('behold, everyone who quotes proverbs will quote this proverb against you: like mother, like daughter'), opens the sisters figure on its own mashal-label onset, הַמֹּשֵׁ֔ל עָלַ֥יִךְ יִמְשֹׁ֖ל (oshb:Ezek.16.44; mashal sweep: 11 verses), rather than a word-event or messenger formula, so the row is closed at 16:43 before that proverb onset begins. MT 16:43 also carries (oshb:Ezek.16.43) a doubled Ketiv/Qere note: the running text reads the ketivs זכרתי and עשיתי, with the Qere layer giving זָכַרְתְּ֙ (oshb:Ezek.16.43, Qere) and עָשִׂית֙ (oshb:Ezek.16.43, Qere).

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:44, already cited as this row's opening verse, introduces the sisters figure ('like mother, like daughter') with no word-event or messenger formula but a clear content-class shift into genealogical comparison (Hittite mother, Amorite father, Samaria and Sodom as sisters, 16:45-46). Close side: MT 16:50 closes the row; its final clause וָאָסִ֥יר אֶתְהֶ֖ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִֽיתִי (oshb:Ezek.16.50) ('so I removed them, as I saw fit') closes the Sodom comparison, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse in the single-witness paragraph layer -- the cleanest mark-corroborated close available inside MT 16.

device_notes: No K/Q note, no paseq record, and no editorial note touch this span.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:51 opens with no formula device, וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י חַטֹּאתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א חָטָ֑אָה וַתַּרְבִּ֤י אֶת תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ מֵהֵ֔נָּה וַתְּצַדְּקִי֙ אֶת אחותך בְּכָל תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עשיתי (oshb:Ezek.16.51), continuing the comparative indictment by default: 'and Samaria did not commit half your sins.' Close side: the row ends at 16:58, the whole verse אֶת זִמָּתֵ֥ךְ וְאֶת תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אַ֣תְּ נְשָׂאתִ֑ים נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.58) ('you bear the penalty of your lewdness and your abominations, declares YHWH'), a verse-final variant close matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse. Two doubled/tripled Ketiv/Qere notes fall inside this span. MT 16:51 reads (oshb:Ezek.16.51) the ketivs אחותך and עשיתי, with the Qere layer giving אֲחוֹתַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Ezek.16.51, Qere) and עָשִֽׂית (oshb:Ezek.16.51, Qere). MT 16:53 carries three notes (oshb:Ezek.16.53) on one verse -- the densest K/Q verse in this span -- reading the ketivs שבית (twice, once before 'Sodom' and once before 'Samaria') and ושבית, against the Qere readings שְׁב֤וּת, שְׁב֥וּת and וּשְׁב֥וּת (all Qere forms of 'fortunes/captivity'). An editorial note also falls at 16:54 inside this span, disclosed as a single-witness vowel-reading divergence, not a text-critical claim about the row's content.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:59 opens with the messenger formula כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.59) ('for thus says the Lord YHWH'), turning from the sisters comparison to YHWH's own covenant memory; the running text reads the ketiv ועשית in place of the pointed form here (oshb:Ezek.16.59). Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own end, MT 16:63, the whole verse לְמַ֤עַן תִּזְכְּרִי֙ וָבֹ֔שְׁתְּ וְלֹ֨א יִֽהְיֶה לָּ֥ךְ עוֹד֙ פִּתְח֣וֹן פֶּ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י כְּלִמָּתֵ֑ךְ בְּכַפְּרִי לָךְ֙ לְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ית נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.63), whose final words are the utterance formula, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse -- the strongest close available in the chapter, mark, refrain and chapter-end all coinciding. Inside the row, MT 16:62 closes with the second-person recognition formula, the whole verse וַהֲקִימוֹתִ֥י אֲנִ֛י אֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.62) ('and you shall know that I am YHWH'), a genuine refrain close that is nonetheless not treated as the row's own end, since 16:63 both continues the same covenant sentence grammatically and carries the stronger, mark-corroborated close.

boundary_rationale: Onset: the dateline at oshb:Ezek.20.1 (וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗ית בַּֽחֲמִשִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ בָּ֧אוּ אֲנָשִׁ֛ים מִזִּקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לִדְרֹ֣שׁ אֶת יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ לְפָנָֽי, the elders come to inquire) opens a narrative frame without its own word-event; the strict word-event formula follows immediately at oshb:Ezek.20.2 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר) as the oracle's sub-onset inside that frame, the same pattern the campaign uses elsewhere for a dateline-only verse. Close: 23:49, whole verse = "וְנָתְנ֤וּ זִמַּתְכֶ֨נָה֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ן וַחֲטָאֵ֥י גִלּוּלֵיכֶ֖ן תִּשֶּׂ֑אינָה וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.23.49)" — ending in a recognition-formula-pattern clause (2mp verb form with the "Lord YHWH" divine-name variant, read directly from these bytes rather than from any pre-counted inventory list), followed by a pe mark (single-witness).

Whole verse = "וַיְהִי֩ דְבַר יְהוָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַתְּשִׁיעִית֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י בֶּעָשׂ֥וֹר לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.24.1)". Close: 24:14 stacks TWO close-grade formulae on one verse — the emphatic "I, YHWH, have spoken" (14-list) and the utterance formula (81-list) — whole verse = "אֲנִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ בָּאָ֣ה וְעָשִׂ֔יתִי לֹֽא אֶפְרַ֥ע וְלֹא אָח֖וּס וְלֹ֣א אֶנָּחֵ֑ם כִּדְרָכַ֤יִךְ וְכַעֲלִילוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ שְׁפָט֔וּךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.24.14)".

boundary_rationale: Onset: 25:1 opens with the word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.25.1) — the strict 39-form and the any-form 41-count both, carrying no dateline. In the WEB, “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.25.1). 25:2 supplies the addressee, "בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.2) — the set-your-face command toward the children of Ammon is the book's first foreign addressee, the class shift that opens the oracles-against-the-nations collection. Close (weighed from both sides): 25:7 ends "לָכֵ֡ן הִנְנִי֩ נָטִ֨יתִי אֶת יָדִ֜י עָלֶ֗יךָ וּנְתַתִּ֤יךָֽ לבג לַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִן הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֖יךָ מִן הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת אַשְׁמִ֣ידְךָ֔ וְיָדַעְתָּ֖ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.7), closing on the 2ms recognition variant "and you shall know that I am YHWH" with a SAMEKH immediately after. An earlier internal close sits at 25:5, "וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת רַבָּה֙ לִנְוֵ֣ה גְמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן לְמִרְבַּץ צֹ֑אן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.5), which also ends on a 2mp recognition-family clause (the wider 2mp recognition family, sweep: 21 verses, includes 25:5, not the strict 2ms list, sweep: 5 verses) and carries its own SAMEKH. Per the standing rule that a refrain closes the unit before it, both 25:5 and 25:7 are treated as closes; they are kept in one row because 25:6 reopens with a coordinating messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה", oshb:Ezek.25.6) against the same addressee (Ammon) rather than a fresh nation, so no addressee-class shift separates 25:5 from 25:7. Ahead of this row, 25:8 opens a fresh messenger formula with an addressee change to Moab, the row's forward hard seam.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 40:1 opens with the dateline בְּאַרְבַּ֤ע עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה אַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכְּתָ֖ה הָעִ֑יר ('after the city was struck') -- the fourteenth and last of the book's fourteen year-bearing datelines -- paired in the same verse with the hand-of-YHWH idiom הָיְתָ֤ה עָלַי֙ יַד יְהוָ֔ה and the transport verb וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה (oshb:Ezek.40.1). This dateline-hand-transport cluster is the strongest onset class the book offers and is also a HARD seam: no row may cross it. It follows immediately, without intervening material, the utterance formula and pe (oshb:Ezek.39.29, single-witness) that close the preceding unit. The frame continues at 40:2 with the header בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֔ים 'in the visions of God' (one of only three such headers in the book) plus a further transport pair (הֱבִיאַ֖נִי / וַיְנִיחֵ֗נִי (oshb:Ezek.40.2)), and again at 40:3 (וַיָּבֵ֨יא אוֹתִ֜י שָׁ֗מָּה (oshb:Ezek.40.3)) introducing the measuring man. Close side: 40:4 carries no formula-grade close device; the seam at 40:4/40:5 rests on the man's charge, הַגֵּ֛ד אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.40.4) 'declare all that you see to the house of Israel', read as ending the entry scene before the measuring reed is put to use in 40:5's וַיָּ֜מָד (oshb:Ezek.40.5), the first of an eighteen-verse run of that verb across 40:5-41:5. Both sides are weighed: the onset is the best-evidenced in the whole span; the close is a content judgment (charge-speech versus measuring-action), not a refrain, and is held accordingly.

The two-verse porch description (40:48-49) is held with the four-verse nave description (41:1-4) as one row rather than left as an under-three-verse fragment. Close side: 41:4 ends with וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֖ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים (oshb:Ezek.41.4) 'he said to me, this is the most holy place', a genuine speak-formula close, before 41:5's fresh measuring verb turns to a new object, the house wall. This close carries a named speech formula rather than resting on content alone, unlike its neighbors on either side.

boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.44.1 opens with a returning-transport verb that reopens the vision frame after the utterance close and double samekh at Ezek.43.27. The prophet is shown the shut east gate and told its meaning (44.2), with the prince's privilege attached (44.3); 44.4 carries a further transport verb (a fresh entry by the north gate) and closes with the prostration formula 'I fell on my face,' matching the vision's own inclusio elsewhere (1.28, 3.23, 11.13, 43.3). Close: the prostration at 44.4 is weighed against the immediately following verse, Ezek.44.5, which opens with a fresh son-of-man address and a directive to mark, see and hear the house's ordinances -- a class shift from vision narrative to statute. boundary_rationale: Onset weighed both sides: Ezek.45.18 carries BOTH a full month+day date formula AND the messenger formula in the same verse -- the exact combination that reads like a fresh oracle onset. On the onset side, the messenger formula (also present at 44.6, 44.9, 45.9, 46.1, 46.16, 47.13) opens what looks like a new speech; but the date clause carries no year word, so it fails the book's structural dateline test (a YEAR word together with a month or day term) -- it is one of exactly four calendar dates in the book (45.18, 45.20, 45.21, 45.25) that carry a month/day construction without a year, and none of the book's fourteen year-bearing datelines falls anywhere across 44.1-48.35. On the close side, the law paragraph before it (45.9-17) already closed at the Ezek.45.17 samekh, and the addressee and topic (the cultic calendar under the temple-law section opened at 45.9) do not change at 45.18 -- there is no addressee-class shift of the kind that would corroborate a fresh onset.
